newsitem.title: USA: Allstate strengthens net loss reserves.
newsitem.headline: Allstate strengthens net loss reserves.

text.p: Allstate Corp said Tuesday it will increase net loss reserves for discontinued lines and coverages by $405 million.
Allstate added that an after-tax charge of $262 million or $0.58 a share for the increased loss reserves will be recorded in the third quarter.

Allstate said it will increase its net loss reserves based on the results of a previously disclosed study of its environmental liabilities as well as a comprehensive internal assessment of its asbestos and other contractual liabilities.

It said the strengthened reserves relate to lines and coverages that Allstate previously discontinued. These consist of excess and surplus insurance, reinsurance and mortgage pool business, which the company no longer writes.
The company said that asbestos loss reserves will be increased by about $75 million and environmental loss reserves by $170 million.
This will bring total net asbestos and environmental reserves to about $1.2 billion.

Allstate also said that loss reserves for other latent exposures and run-off businesses will be increased by $160 million. Run-off businesses are insurance operations that Allstate no longer writes coverage for, but may be subject to existing and potential claims.

"This action to strengthen our reserves follows several repositioning activities we've recently undertaken to enhance our financial position and focus on the company's core businesses of auto, home and life insurance," Allstate Chairman Jerry Choate said in a statement. "In the past year, Allstate has sold those operations that do not fit with our strategic direction, and set in motion programs to reduce our catastrophe exposure in California and Florida."

Allstate said it believes its reserves for environmental and asbestos coverages are appropriate, but the ultimate cost of claims may vary due to court decisions, litigation and other uncertainties. Due to these variables, the insurance company said management believes it is not feasible to develop a meaningful range for additional reserves that may be required.
